contract.description: Outcome-blind task-design annotations extracted from the cited Methods sections.
contract.distance_rule: Equal-weight Gower/Hamming mismatch, minimized over the three source-task prototypes. A list-valued annotation matches when either task value overlaps the prototype value. No weights or annotations use GRU results.

tier_reasons.primary: Complete retained cohorts with valid matched splits and adequate cross-cohort comparability.
tier_reasons.stress_test: Valid splits retained as scientifically useful boundary cases, but treatment, lesion, or strongly different task structure limits direct comparability.
tier_reasons.descriptive_only: Valid split, but the released sample is too small for cross-cohort inference.
tier_reasons.quarantined: The frozen result violates the intended within-condition transfer estimand and is excluded from every correlation, ranking, and direction count.

kwak.reason: The current manifest adapts on CNO sessions and tests on DMSO sessions, confounding subject adaptation with treatment transfer.
kwak.split_contract: Retain DMSO/control sessions only for every subject; adapt on chronological odd-indexed DMSO sessions and test on chronological even-indexed DMSO sessions. Never adapt on one treatment and score another treatment.

grossman.evidence_note: Head-restrained mice chose left/right lick spouts; independent water probabilities changed in blocks.

chen.evidence_note: Freely moving mice nose-poked one of two touchscreen targets for liquid Ensure under independent restless schedules.

zid.evidence_note: Online participants chose between two card decks for points with independently evolving reward probabilities.

lebedeva.evidence_note: Head-fixed mice turned a wheel left/right for water under complementary 80/20 reversals.

beron.evidence_note: Freely moving mice chose left/right ports for water in a latent-state probabilistic reversal task.

kwak.evidence_note: Freely moving mice nose-poked left/right ports for water; each arm probability was constant within blocks and changed without cues.

miller.evidence_note: Rats repeatedly selected two nose ports for small liquid rewards while both reinforcement probabilities changed continuously.

findling.evidence_note: Human participants used handheld buttons to choose visual shapes with randomized screen position, 85/15 reversals, and euro feedback.

tang.evidence_note: Head-restrained macaques made saccades in action- and object-value blocks for juice under 70/30 reversals.

alsio.evidence_note: Freely moving rats performed spatial and visual touchscreen reversals for food pellets; contingencies reversed after a criterion.

eckstein.evidence_note: Human participants selected left/right boxes by keyboard in a stochastic reversal task with points/coin feedback.

costa.evidence_note: Head-restrained macaques chose randomized-position visual stimuli by saccade for apple juice under 80/20, 70/30, or 60/40 reversals.

lopez_mouse.evidence_note: Freely moving mice nose-poked left/right ports for water under baited variable-interval schedules with blockwise set rates.
